title: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head J (Ministry of Defence)

sections.label: National Service Bill 1967
sections.summary: In 1967 he moved the National Service Bill asking why defend Singapore if it was said to be indefensible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 1967, he moved the National Service Bill with a stark question: why defend Singapore at all, if this island was said to be indefensible?

sections.label: Defence questions on risks and diplomacy
sections.summary: Three questions ask how MINDEF's risk assessment evolved, how Total Defence is strengthened, and how defence diplomacy widens strategic space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, how has MINDEF's assessment of security conflicts and risks evolved over the past five years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, how are we strengthening Total Defence as a whole to prepare Singaporeans for crises and contingencies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, how is defence diplomacy widening our strategic space while safeguarding our Independence?

sections.label: SAF 2040 on technological change
sections.summary: SAF 2040 recognises that technological change is compressing decision cycles and expanding the battlespace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: SAF 2040 recognises that technological change is compressing decision cycles and expanding the battlespace.

sections.label: Singapore defence force and partnerships
sections.summary: Singapore anchors security in a strong defence force and diversified defence partnerships, including the US, Australia and the Five Power Defence Arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's long-standing strategy has been to anchor our security in a strong defence force, supported by a diversified network of defence partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our close relationships with countries, such as the United States (US) and Australia, have enabled us to expand our training arrangements and to enhance our military's readiness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Five Power Defence Arrangements continues to provide a practical and flexible platform for interoperability through regular exercises.

sections.label: Counterterrorism and maritime information-sharing
sections.summary: Singapore strengthened counterterrorism information-sharing through the ASEAN Our Eyes Initiative and contributes to the Information Fusion Centre for maritime threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In counterterrorism, Singapore has strengthened information-sharing with regional partners to enhance collective early warning capabilities, including through the ASEAN Our Eyes Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In maritime security, Singapore contributes to the Information Fusion Centre, which facilitates timely information sharing on maritime threats.

sections.label: State-based armed conflicts in 2024
sections.summary: In 2024 there were 61 state-based armed conflicts worldwide, the highest number recorded since the Second World War.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2024, there were 61 state-based armed conflicts worldwide – the highest number recorded since the Second World War.

sections.label: Ukraine naval drones Black Sea
sections.summary: Ukraine used low-cost naval drones to break Russia's Black Sea blockade and force the Russian fleet to withdraw from Crimea without conventional warships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Ukraine has even used low-cost naval drones to break Russia's Black Sea blockade and force the withdrawal of the Russian fleet from Crimea, a remarkable feat achieved without conventional warships.

sections.label: DSTA SAF unmanned systems
sections.summary: DSTA has pivoted toward robotics, drones, autonomy and AI, and the SAF and Air Force set up counter-UAS and UAS warfare groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA) has already pivoted decisively toward robotics, drones, autonomy and AI, recognising that the proliferation of drones and autonomous systems is reshaping the physical domain while cyberattacks and disinformation are transforming the digital space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The SAF has established a Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) Development and Operations group and the Air Force has set up a new UAS Warfare and Tactics Centre to drive the development and integration of unmanned platforms across all services.

sections.label: Question on emerging battlefield technologies
sections.summary: The member asks the Minister for an update on strategies against emerging and disruptive battlefield technologies and ensuring Singapore's security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given these rapidly evolving threats and opportunities, I would like to ask the Minister for an update on our strategies to guard against such emerging and disruptive technologies that can be used on the battlefield and how we will ensure that Singapore remains secure in this era of warfare.

sections.label: Drone costs and SAF unmanned training
sections.summary: The member notes a $20,000 drone can destroy million-dollar infrastructure and asks how SAF uses unmanned technology in training given falling birth rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: A drone costing around $20,000 can potentially destroy infrastructure worth millions while forcing defenders to use missiles costing hundreds of thousands of dollars to intercept it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: First, in light of Singapore's falling birth rate, may I ask the Minister, how is SAF using unmanned technology in local and overseas training to improve effectiveness and reduce manpower reliance?

sections.label: MINDEF unmanned systems manpower savings
sections.summary: The member asks MINDEF's projected percentage manpower savings from unmanned systems to mitigate the declining population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: What is MINDEF's projected percentage manpower savings from the use of unmanned systems to mitigate the declining population?

sections.label: Digital and Intelligence Service update
sections.summary: The member asks for an update on how the DIS builds cyber capabilities, talent pipelines, and industry and academia partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The establishment of the Digital and Intelligence Service (DIS) in 2022 marked a significant milestone in strengthening our defence posture in the digital domain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on how the DIS is building deep cyber capabilities, strengthening talent pipelines, and partnering industry and academia to stay ahead of emerging threats?

sections.label: Defence spending projection and cost effectiveness
sections.summary: Asks for defence spending projections this year and how MINDEF and SAF ensure cost effectiveness in procurements and programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, what is the projection for defence spending this year in absolute terms and as a share of Government expenditure and gross domestic product (GDP), and what are the key drivers of any change?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Second, how does MINDEF and the SAF ensure cost effectiveness across major procurements and long-term programmes?

sections.label: Supply chain diversification and contract accountability
sections.summary: Asks how MINDEF diversifies supply sources, uses claw back clauses and liquidated damages, and gives AGO audit access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How is MINDEF diversifying and sourcing from a wider range of global partners to mitigate single point failures in the supply chain?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does MINDEF have a robust claw back clauses and does it provide for liquidated damages for delays within these high-end contracts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Furthermore, MINDEF must ensure that multi-billion-dollar high-end contracts are transparent and accountable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This can be done by ensuring the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) is given full access to audit procurement milestones, contract variations and delivery timelines.

sections.label: MINDEF talent growth programmes
sections.summary: MINDEF has programmes to grow talent from within, including the Sentinel Programme, Cyber Work-Learn Scheme and enhanced expertise deployment scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MINDEF has programmes to grow talent from within – the Sentinel Programme for youths, the Cyber Work-Learn Scheme for Full-time National Servicemen (NSFs), the enhanced expertise deployment scheme for national servicemen with relevant civilian skills.

sections.label: UK cyber recruitment terms and results
sections.summary: Describes UK cyber recruitment with one-month basic training, waived standards, over $40,000 salary, and 30 recruits defending networks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Basic training cut to one month, fitness and medical standards waived, no formal qualifications required, demonstrated skills sufficient, starting salary over $40,000 pounds, with up to $25,000 in additional skills pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first cohort of 30 entered operational roles in late 2025, helping defend UK networks against 90,000 attacks over two years.

sections.label: Second year NSF allowance increase cost
sections.summary: Raising second year NSF allowances to $1,800 LQS with CPF would cost $150 to $200 million yearly, under 1% of defence budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Raising second year NSF allowances to the new Local Qualifying Salary (LQS) of $1,800 with employer CPF would cost approximately $150 to $200 million a year, under 1% of a $25 billion defence budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I ask the Minister: will the Ministry commit to at least the LQS of $1,800 for second year NSFs?

sections.label: Singapore defence cooperation and reliance safeguards
sections.summary: Asks how Singapore will strengthen defence cooperation with multiple partners and what safeguards prevent over-reliance on any single partnership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: In an increasingly complex and multipolar world, Singapore has to maintain the flexibility to work with multiple partners while preserving our sovereignty and independence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: How will Singapore strengthen defence cooperation not only with the US and China, but also with other key strategic partners in our region and beyond, whether through joint exercises, military exchanges, technology collaboration, defence industry partnerships or crisis communication mechanisms?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: What safeguards are in place to ensure that we do not become overly reliant to any single defence partnership?

sections.label: Total Defence in Singapore security
sections.summary: Total Defence has played a significant role in Singapore's security over the past 42 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Total Defence has played a significant role in Singapore's security over the past 42 years.

sections.label: Update on Total Defence activities
sections.summary: A question asks MINDEF for an update on participation and outcomes from Total Defence activities like Exercise SG Ready this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could MINDEF please provide an update on participation and outcomes from Total Defence related activities, like Exercise SG Ready, this year?

sections.label: Changes in security environment
sections.summary: In recent years, the security environment has seen three major changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In recent years, the security environment has seen three major changes.

sections.label: Technology changing defence building
sections.summary: Technology is rapidly changing the way defence is built.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, technology is rapidly changing the way defence is built.

sections.label: Enlistment Act and National Service
sections.summary: The Enlistment Act requires males over 18 to have compulsory NS in SAF, SPF or SCDF, and NS has evolved beyond defence into social fabric.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, the Enlistment Act requires males of over 18 years old to have compulsory NS – SAF, SPF or the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NS as an institution has already evolved beyond protection and the defence of Singapore, but also as a social fabric for us to bond together, to understand each other, whether it is race or culture.

sections.label: Voluntary services as National Service
sections.summary: A question asks whether such services can be seen not as purely voluntary but as an extension of National Service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is it possible for us to not look at this type of services as just purely voluntary services but as an extension of our National Service?

sections.label: SAFVC roles and volunteers
sections.summary: The SAFVC, started in 2014, lets new citizens, first-generation PRs, women and those without NS obligations serve in over 30 roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, started in 2014, the SAFVC stands as a vital avenue for new citizens, first‑generation PRs, Singaporean women and those without NS obligations to step forward, serve alongside our NSFs, NSmen and Regulars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SAFVC has grown steadily, offering more than 30 meaningful roles across the Army, Navy, Air Force and the DIS – from security, naval operations to engineering and legal work.

sections.label: SAFVC 10th anniversary volunteers
sections.summary: The SAFVC marks its 10th anniversary, a decade in which over 1,500 volunteers stepped forward to serve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Celebrating its 10th anniversary, a decade that saw over 1,500 volunteers that stepped forward to serve.

sections.label: SAFVC at Exercise Wallaby
sections.summary: Last year the SAFVC first joined Exercise Wallaby, with Forward Support Group volunteers providing medical, logistics, maintenance and transportation support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, the SAFVC also participated for the first time in Exercise Wallaby, Singapore's largest unilateral overseas military exercise, where volunteers in the Forward Support Group provided medical, logistics, maintenance and transportation support to the training units.

sections.label: SAFVC expansion and SAFRA clubs
sections.summary: It asks how SAFVC will expand volunteerism and roles, and notes SAFRA, since 1972, now has seven clubs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, as Singapore's society becomes more diverse and as more individuals without formal NS obligations express the desire to serve, the question is, how will SAFVC expand opportunities for volunteerism and what new roles could emerge to meet evolving operational needs from cyber and data to medical, logistics and community engagement?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Since 1972, the Singapore Armed Forces Reservists Association (SAFRA) has been more than just a provider of gyms and swimming pools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Today, with seven clubs spanning from Jurong to Punggol, SAFRA stands as a tangible thank you from the nation to those who serve.

sections.label: Choa Chu Kang clubhouse and NS habits
sections.summary: It notes the new Choa Chu Kang clubhouse and asks what initiatives or infrastructure improvements the NS community can look forward to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While the new Choa Chu Kang clubhouse is a masterpiece of modern integration, our NSFs and pre-enlistees have different digital and social habits compared to my generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: What upcoming initiatives or infrastructure improvements can the NS community look forward to?

sections.label: SAFRA engaging public on defence
sections.summary: It asks whether SAFRA's network and facilities can be used to engage the wider Singapore public on defence matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can we leverage SAFRA's network and facilities to engage the wider Singapore public on defence matters?

sections.label: MINDEF partnerships with SAFRA
sections.summary: The question asks how MINDEF can deepen partnerships with organisations like SAFRA beyond recreation facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My question therefore is how MINDEF can deepen partnerships with organisations like SAFRA so that they go beyond just being facilities for recreation.

sections.label: Total Defence community anchoring outcomes
sections.summary: The passage asks what outcomes MINDEF will track to assess whether defence is anchored in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If we are intentional in leveraging the reach and influence of institutions like SAFRA, we can ensure that Total Defence can remain a lived national commitment and not confined to the uniformed services or to our schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would appreciate if the Ministry could share what outcomes MINDEF will track to assess whether defence is truly anchored in the community and what more can be done to strengthen this vital pillar of national resilience.

sections.label: SAFRA clubhouses and members
sections.summary: SAFRA has seven clubhouses and over 475,000 members, with Exercise SG Ready 2026 activities held at clubhouses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Today, SAFRA has seven clubhouses spread across Singapore and more than 475,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: For example, just earlier this month, as part of Exercise SG Ready 2026, simulated disruption activities and programmes to commemorate Total Defence were held at SAFRA clubhouses for NSmen and their families to learn about readiness for power outages and disrupted digital connectivity.

sections.label: Leveraging SAFRA infrastructure for Total Defence
sections.summary: The question asks whether MINDEF plans to leverage SAFRA's infrastructure and network to raise Total Defence awareness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the premises, I would like to ask the Minister whether MINDEF have plans to better leverage SAFRA's existing infrastructure and network to build stronger ties and raise Total Defence awareness in the community.

sections.label: Singapore's strategic realities
sections.summary: Singapore's strategic realities are its geography, manpower and constrained resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore's strategic realities are our geography, manpower and constrained resources.

sections.label: Small population and defence force
sections.summary: With its small population size, Singapore cannot rely on a fully Regular or volunteer force large enough for defence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: With our small population size, we can never rely on a fully Regular or volunteer force large enough for our defence needs.

sections.label: International order and norms
sections.summary: This order prioritised collective problem-solving, rules of behaviour in the global commons and guardrails against military escalation, but countries can no longer be expected to work within international laws and norms by default.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This order prioritised collective problem-solving and rules of behaviour in the global commons, as well as serving as guardrails against military escalation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: However, we can no longer expect countries to work within international laws and norms as a default.

sections.label: Pressure on Singapore's sovereignty
sections.summary: For small countries like Singapore, this shift puts pressure on our autonomy and sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For small countries like Singapore, this shift puts pressure on our autonomy and sovereignty.

sections.label: Reliance on ourselves
sections.summary: The world does not owe Singapore a living or its survival, so it can rely only on itself and not on anyone else's security guarantees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The world does not owe us a living or our survival.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We can rely only on ourselves and not on the security guarantees of anyone else.

sections.label: SAF capabilities beyond war
sections.summary: The SAF must have calibrated options for scenarios beyond and below the threshold of war, so MINDEF/SAF will build conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But the SAF must also have other calibrated options in response to an expanded range of scenarios beyond and below the threshold of war.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is why MINDEF/SAF will build up a suite of capabilities comprising: conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities.

sections.label: RSAF maritime surveillance aircraft
sections.summary: The RSAF will acquire three Gulfstream G550-Maritime Surveillance Aircraft to complement the Boeing P-8A Maritime Patrol Aircraft.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, the RSAF will acquire three Gulfstream G550-Maritime Surveillance Aircraft (MSA), to complement the Boeing P-8A Maritime Patrol Aircraft.

sections.label: Second MRCV launch
sections.summary: The second MRCV is on track to be launched in the third quarter of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The second MRCV is on track to be launched in the third quarter of 2026.

sections.label: CyTEC repositioned as experimentation centre
sections.summary: The DIS will reposition the Cyber Defence Test and Evaluation Centre as a Cyber Defence Test and Experimentation Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The DIS will thus reposition the Cyber Defence Test and Evaluation Centre (CyTEC) as a Cyber Defence Test and Experimentation Centre.

sections.label: Second MMRC at Bedok Camp
sections.summary: The Army will build a second MMRC at Bedok Camp, freeing land from six baffled ranges and letting NSmen book ranges via the OneNS app.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For more of our soldiers to use such facilities, the Army will build a second MMRC at Bedok Camp.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MMRC 2 will free up land currently occupied by six baffled ranges, which can be repurposed for our other training needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It will also be easier for our soldiers to train at MMRC 2 NSmen can simply book ranges for training conveniently through the OneNS app without having to go through their parent unit.

sections.label: Defence technology community and industries
sections.summary: Defence must include the defence and technology community and defence industries, with investment in DSO and DSTA and local industry providing resilience and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Beyond the Army, Air Force, Navy and DIS, it must also include our defence and technology community, and it must also include our defence industries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have judiciously invested in the DSO National Laboratories and DSTA over the years, building a corps of scientists and engineers with expertise that money cannot buy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our local defence industry gives us resilience, the ability to scale and, most importantly, the ability to develop capabilities that we cannot buy.

sections.label: Defence spending growth to keep pace
sections.summary: Defence spending growth is expected to keep pace with GDP barring major shocks, with readiness to spend more if needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Going forward, I expect the growth in defence spending to keep pace with GDP, barring major shocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: However, if the need arises, we are prepared to spend more.

sections.label: Review of Medical Classification System
sections.summary: MINDEF will review the Medical Classification System to be more precise, better characterising servicemen's medical fitness and its effect on tasks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To this end, MINDEF will review our Medical Classification System to be more precise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This will allow better characterisation of the medical fitness of our servicemen, and how that affects their ability to undertake various tasks.

sections.label: NSmen organised into cyber defence teams
sections.summary: The DIS will better organise national servicemen with relevant cyber expertise into Sectoral Cyber Defence Teams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The DIS will thus better organise our national servicemen with relevant cyber expertise, into Sectoral Cyber Defence Teams.

sections.label: SAF NSmen support rings
sections.summary: The second ring is 250,000 mobilisable NSmen, and the third is 750,000 former NSmen plus 2.5 million families and employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The second ring is the SAF's full-force potential, comprising 250,000 NSmen who can be mobilised when required.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The third ring of support is the wider NS community – comprising some 750,000 former NSmen, as well as the 2.5 million families and employers supporting them.

sections.label: Defence Volunteer Ecosystem strengthening
sections.summary: MINDEF will strengthen the Defence Volunteer Ecosystem through the SG Defence Volunteer Network and SAFVC, as more volunteers increase deterrence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And the more Singaporeans who volunteer with their time and service, the more powerful our deterrence will be.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: That is why MINDEF will strengthen the Defence Volunteer Ecosystem through the SG Defence Volunteer Network and SAFVC.

sections.label: Underwater infrastructure defence partnerships
sections.summary: Singapore taps Finland, Estonia and the Netherlands for underwater infrastructure defence principles, and MINDEF diversifies partnerships to mitigate supply chain failures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: On critical underwater infrastructure specifically, we are tapping the expertise of newer partners, like Finland, Estonia and the Netherlands, to develop principles and best practices for defence cooperation that can be adapted to our region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: MINDEF has been diversifying our global partnerships to mitigate single-point supply chain failures.

sections.label: Expanded defence tech partnerships
sections.summary: Singapore has expanded defence tech partnerships with various countries, with increased interest through initiatives like the Defence Industry Day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For instance, we have expanded our defence tech partnerships with various countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Recently, we have seen an increased interest by various countries to partner Singapore through initiatives, like the Defence Industry Day, where we bring together the defence industries of different countries.

sections.label: Whole-of-society defence and complacency
sections.summary: Defence belongs to all of society, and advanced capabilities and billions in infrastructure count for nothing if complacency causes fundamental surprise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is so that we can develop value propositions to work with them in the evolving context.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But as I have stated earlier, defence cannot be achieved by MINDEF/SAF alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It belongs to the whole of society – to every Singaporean, in every sector, in every community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We can train with the most advanced capabilities, invest billions in our defence infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But all of that will count for nothing if we are not vigilant, if we allow ourselves to be fundamentally surprised because we have been lulled into complacency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The recent conflicts have presented many examples where, even when confronted with clear intelligence of threats, capable and technologically advanced militaries failed to respond because they convinced themselves that it would not happen to them or that it could not happen to them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They did not fail in technology, equipping or training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They failed to challenge their mindsets, they failed to guard against complacency, and they fell into denial of the harsh possibilities of conflict.

sections.label: Early enlistment Work-Learn Schemes
sections.summary: Since 2023, Work-Learn Schemes let selected polytechnic students enlist a year early.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since 2023, we have created Work-Learn Schemes that let selected polytechnic students enlist a year early.

sections.label: SAF Work-Learn Schemes
sections.summary: Ten Work-Learn Schemes have been introduced, focusing on areas vital to SAF capabilities including AI and engineering.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: They focus on areas vital to SAF capabilities – AI, engineering and others.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We have introduced 10 Work-Learn Schemes to date.

sections.label: NS certificates in Skills Passport
sections.summary: MINDEF and SAF are partnering SkillsFuture Singapore to include NS certificates in the Careers and Skills Passport.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MINDEF and SAF are partnering SkillsFuture Singapore to include NS certificates in the Careers and Skills Passport.

sections.label: NS servicemen payouts
sections.summary: Servicemen receive up to $6,500 upon completing full-time NS, about $5,500 of it CPF, and up to $18,500 after Operationally Ready NS training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Servicemen receive up to $6,500 upon completion of full-time NS – on the question of CPF, of that amount, CPF comes to about $5,500 – and up to $18,500 total after completing their Operationally Ready NS training.

sections.label: NS not employer-employee relationship
sections.summary: Serving NS involves opportunity cost, but casting it as an employer-employee relationship should not erode the social compact and ethos of service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: While we acknowledge that serving NS involves opportunity cost, we should not erode our social compact and the ethos of service by casting it as an employer-employee relationship.

sections.label: NSmen redeployed to expertise roles
sections.summary: About 850 NSmen have been redeployed into roles better aligned with their professional expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: About 850 NSmen have been redeployed into roles better aligned with their professional expertise.

sections.label: NSmen in Sectoral Cyber Defence Teams
sections.summary: From June this year, the SAF will deploy NSmen with cyber expertise into Sectoral Cyber Defence Teams.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: From June this year, the SAF will deploy NSmen with cyber expertise into Sectoral Cyber Defence Teams.

sections.label: SG Defence Volunteer Network
sections.summary: MINDEF and SAF will establish the SG Defence Volunteer Network this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MINDEF and SAF will establish the SG Defence Volunteer Network this year.

sections.label: National Education Ambassadors
sections.summary: MINDEF now has more than 100 National Education Ambassadors from various professional backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: MINDEF now has more than 100 National Education Ambassadors from various professional backgrounds.

sections.label: SAFVC volunteers trained and serving
sections.summary: More than 1,500 SAFVC volunteers have been trained and served Singapore since its formation, and the SAFVC will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since its formation, more than 1,500 SAFVC volunteers have been trained and served Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Moving ahead, we will enhance the SAFVC to enable more people to serve in a wider range of roles.

sections.label: New non-uniformed military volunteer scheme
sections.summary: A new non-uniformed military volunteer scheme with new roles will be introduced, welcoming Singaporean women, new citizens and PRs aged 18 to 45.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This shows how more of our volunteer schemes can be put to support the core of the SAF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will also introduce a new non-uniformed military volunteer scheme with new roles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As we expand these opportunities, we welcome Singaporean women, new citizens and PRs aged 18 to 45 who wish to serve.

sections.label: Exercise SG Ready participation
sections.summary: This year's Exercise SG Ready was held over two weeks earlier this month, with more than 1,000 agencies, businesses and community organisations taking part.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Members in this House and their residents can also participate to prepare our communities and households for such situations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This year's Exercise SG Ready was held over two weeks earlier this month, with more than 1,000 agencies, businesses and community organisations taking part.

sections.label: Business Continuity Plans and phishing exercise
sections.summary: Over 500 organisations revised their Business Continuity Plans and close to 140 companies participated in a phishing exercise with more than 8,500 emails sent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Over 500 organisations revised their Business Continuity Plans and close to 140 companies participated in a phishing exercise which saw more than 8,500 phishing emails sent to employees.

sections.label: Total Defence responsibility for everyone
sections.summary: Defence is transformed from the duty of national servicemen and Regulars into the responsibility of everyone, including women, PRs and new citizens who volunteer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, we are transforming defence from the duty of our national servicemen and our Regulars, into the responsibility of everyone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To our national servicemen and Regulars, your service remains our foundation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To every woman, PR and new citizen ready to serve, your commitment to volunteer contributes to our Total Defence efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Together, we do not just defend our sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We defend the Singapore promise, that everyone who calls this home has a part in keeping it safe.

sections.label: SAFRA's evolving defence role
sections.summary: SAFRA's role in strengthening Singapore's defence ecosystem is outlined as transforming from a social club into part of a nation-wide defence movement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Today, I will outline SAFRA's evolving role in strengthening Singapore's defence ecosystem, transforming from what was once seen primarily as a social club into a part of a vital, nation-wide defence movement.

sections.label: SAFRA clubhouse and membership expansion
sections.summary: SAFRA expanded its network of seven clubhouses across Singapore and now serves more than 400,000 members, including NSFs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Over the following decades, SAFRA expanded to increase accessibility, increasing its network of seven clubhouses across Singapore to now serving more than 400,000 members, including NSFs.

sections.label: SAFRA must become community bridge
sections.summary: SAFRA must evolve beyond providing lifestyle and recreational facilities to become a bridge connecting citizen soldiers with the broader community they protect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: But as our operating environment evolves, SAFRA too must evolve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: It cannot remain only a provider of lifestyle and recreational facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: It must become a bridge, connecting our citizen soldiers with the broader community they protect.

sections.label: SkillsFuture@NS Fairs for NS transition
sections.summary: For those transitioning after full-time NS, SAFRA hosts quarterly SkillsFuture@NS Fairs connecting them with career and education opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: For those transitioning after full-time NS, SAFRA hosts quarterly SkillsFuture@NS Fairs that connect them with career and education opportunities.

sections.label: SAFRA NS Experience camps
sections.summary: SAFRA currently runs two types of NS Experience camps, the BMT Kids Camp and the NS Family Experience Camp, to bridge a gap.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: To bridge this gap, SAFRA currently runs two types of NS Experience camps: the BMT Kids Camp and the NS Family Experience Camp.

sections.label: SAFRA expands NS Experience camps
sections.summary: SAFRA will expand its partnership with the SAF and other organisations to develop new NS Experience camp variants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Building on this success, SAFRA will expand its partnership with the SAF and other organisations to develop new variants of the NS Experience camp.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: This includes a one-day NS for Everyone programme and a two-day Empowering NS for Women camp.

sections.label: NSman volunteers financial planning
sections.summary: Since 2023, LTC(NS) William Koh has volunteered financial planning expertise, benefiting over 650 fellow NSmen through workshops and coaching.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: For example, since 2023, one NSman, LTC(NS) William Koh, has volunteered his expertise in financial planning, benefiting over 650 fellow NSmen through workshops and one-on-one coaching.

sections.label: SAFRA Community Defence Festival
sections.summary: The inaugural SAFRA Community Defence and Resilience Festival will be held in early 2027 at multiple sites, engaging up to 80,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: The public can look forward to the inaugural SAFRA Community Defence and Resilience Festival in early 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: To be held at multiple sites across Singapore, this Festival will feature defence-themed activities for the masses, engaging up to 80,000 participants.

sections.label: SAFRA expands community defence pathways
sections.summary: SAFRA will expand NSmen regional engagement opportunities and create pathways for youths, women and community members to contribute to defence initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: SAFRA will expand opportunities for NSmen to lead regional engagement efforts, strengthening ties between defence and community networks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: In partnership with Nexus’ Engagement and Volunteer Office and as part of the broader SG Defence Volunteers Network which Senior Minister of State Zaqy had mentioned earlier, SAFRA will also create pathways for youths, women and other members of the community to contribute to defence-related initiatives.

sections.label: SAFRA bridges NSmen and community
sections.summary: SAFRA's evolution aims to help every Singaporean understand their stake in defence, with SAFRA as a bridge to the wider community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: In the face of new and evolving security challenges, NS is vital to our nation’s survival.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: SAFRA’s evolution is about helping every Singaporean understand their stake in our nation’s defence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: We will achieve this with SAFRA serving as a bridge connecting our citizen soldiers with the wider community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: When NSmen volunteer in their communities, when families participate in defence activities, when businesses support our servicemen, we create a nation where defence truly becomes everyone’s mission.

sections.label: Capabilities revealed when useful
sections.summary: The speaker does not intend to list conventional capabilities and timelines, revealing them only when operationally useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, I do not intend to list out all the conventional capabilities and their timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: As I mentioned, we will only reveal the capabilities at a time of our choosing, when it is operationally useful.

sections.label: Mix of response capabilities
sections.summary: Responding to expanded scenarios requires a mix of conventional, classified, cyber and cheap asymmetric capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Within these expanded scenarios and each of the different scenarios, we will need a mix of different capabilities to respond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That includes what we call conventional capabilities, classified capabilities, cyber capabilities and including the cheap asymmetric capabilities.

sections.label: Second-hand C130 acquisition
sections.summary: Four second-hand C130 were acquired to be refurbished for operational needs and to stretch the defence dollar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, recently, we have acquired four second-hand C130 to be refurbished to meet our operational needs, to stretch our defence dollar.

sections.label: Ballistic missiles in Southeast Asia
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to assess weapon types new to Southeast Asia, specifically modern ballistic missiles after Indonesia's KHAN acquisition from Türkiye.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: First on capabilities, as we modernise the SAF, what is the Minister's assessment of the introduction of weapon types not previously present in Southeast Asia, specifically modern ballistic missiles, following Indonesia's acquisition of the KHAN from Türkiye?

sections.label: Non-disclosure of threat scenarios
sections.summary: The ballistic missile threat is not new, and specific threat scenarios and operational responses are not discussed in the Chamber.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, ballistic missiles threat is not new, and it can emanate from within and beyond this region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second thing I will say is that we do not discuss specific threat scenarios in this Chamber, because we do not want to make it a self-fulfilling prophecy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Number three, we do not discuss specific operational response in this Chamber either, because we do not need others to know what we can do and where our gaps might be.

sections.label: Care for NSmen and NSFs
sections.summary: NSmen and NSFs will be taken care of in consultation with the Ministry of Finance where budget space allows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And it is not just about NSF allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will take care of our NSmen, we will take care of our NSFs in consultation with the Ministry of Finance, where the budget space allows.

sections.label: NS credits and duty
sections.summary: More will be done for NS credits and tax incentives, but Members are urged not to conflate duty with transaction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Of course, we will do more for the NS credits, the tax incentive, wherever we can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But I appeal to Members of this House not to conflate duty with transaction.

sections.label: Agencies in cyber attacks
sections.summary: In recent cyber attacks, agencies involved include MINDEF, MHA, Cyber Security Agency of Singapore, Infocomm Media Development Authority and other related sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, in the recent cyber attacks that we have seen, the agencies involved will include assets and capabilities from MINDEF, MHA, the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore, the Infocomm Media Development Authority and also other various related sectors.

sections.label: Building agency capabilities against attacks
sections.summary: Government deploys resources to help agencies build capabilities, conducting exercises and trainings with telcos, as defence strength depends on the weakest link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: What we also need to do as a whole-of-Government is to deploy our resources to help our various agencies build up their capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, for example, in the recent issue with the CII, while we are managing the incident real time, we are also conducting exercises and trainings to help the various telco to build up their capabilities, because at the end of the day when an attack is on a part of the network, the strength of our defence is always contingent on the weakest link and we want to level up the capabilities across the entire nation.

sections.label: Response after successful terrorist attacks
sections.summary: After a successful terrorist attack killing someone or bombing somewhere, they ensured the place was cleaned up within hours and life continued normally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Whenever they are faced with a terrorist attack, and if the terrorist were successful in killing someone or bombing somewhere, they made it a point that within a few hours, they will make sure that the place is entirely cleaned up and people will go on with their life as per normal.

sections.label: Auditing MINDEF defence procurement
sections.summary: MINDEF's audit system is multi-layered and robust, with a system to audit classified projects to ensure money is well spent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: How does MINDEF ensure that even the most expensive defence procurement, including lifecycle cost and delivery timeline, is properly audited, while ensuring that operational secrecy is not compromised?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Second, in view of emergent and evolving threats, is MINDEF looking beyond the DSTA, DSO and ST Engineering to collaborate with local entrepreneurs on dual use technologies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Chair, let me first assure Members of this House that the audit system in MINDEF is multi-layered and robust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Even for classified projects, there is a system for us to audit classified projects to make sure that money is well spent.

sections.label: After-sales service and platform lifecycle
sections.summary: MINDEF wants after-sales service and assurance of capability, spares and technical ability to upgrade platforms for 20 years and beyond, even if the supplier goes away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Many countries, many militaries will buy things upfront.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We want to make sure that there is a after-sales service and we want to assure ourselves if the lifecycle of that platform is for 20 years, we have the capability and the assurance and the spares to make sure that, that will work for 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Even if one day the supplier goes away, we must have the technical capability to continue to upgrade those platforms for the 20 years and beyond.

sections.label: Protecting shared technology intellectual property
sections.summary: When securing technologies, intellectual property must be protected and the conditions upon which technologies were shared must be respected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: When we secure any technologies, we must also protect the intellectual property and respect the conditions upon which those technologies have been shared with us.

sections.label: Collective cyber defence
sections.summary: A cyberattack on one part of the system is an attack on the entire network, and defence is better done collectively with partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: A cyberattack on one part of the system is an attack on the entire network and we will pitch to other partners that our defence is better when we do it collectively.

sections.label: Critical underwater infrastructure norms
sections.summary: Singapore seeks like-minded partners to develop norms for protecting critical underwater infrastructure, given an international legal lacuna.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today we have heard of many stories of the challenges that the European countries face, the Middle Eastern countries face.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And now we are thinking through how we can convene like-minded partners to come together to develop some norms for the protection of our critical underwater infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Because under international laws there is a lacuna on what can be done and who should be responsible for what.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But we have heard enough interest from our partners from Australia, New Zealand, North East Asia, Europe and even America, to want to talk about this topic and to explore how we can work collectively to share information, share best practices and perhaps, narrow the international legal lacuna.

sections.label: EnergyOne gym training
sections.summary: EnergyOne gym staff are capable former personnel who incorporated military training, and the clubhouse will move to where people are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: In fact, at EnergyOne, the people running our gym, they are very capable people who have served before and who understood the requirements of military training and incorporated training to suit the people joining in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: It is our vision that we will extend and move the clubhouse to where the people are.

sections.label: Contributing to Singapore's relevance
sections.summary: The speaker encourages everyone in the Public Service and SAF to contribute to strengthening Singapore's relevance to the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Chair, I thank Mr Yip for his clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have a simple rule that I encourage everyone in the Public Service, and all the men and women at SAF to do, to contribute to how Singapore can continue to strengthen our relevance to the world.

sections.label: Realistic view of powers
sections.summary: Singapore does not take a moralistic attitude to other countries' foreign policy or military posture but a realistic view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We do not take a moralistic attitude towards other people's foreign policy or military posture, but I take a very realistic view of what they do and to understand why they do what they do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, for the US, China and other middle powers, we never take it as a given that they will continue to want to engage with Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: What has worked in the past may no longer work, going forward.

sections.label: Reliability, trustworthiness, capability
sections.summary: Nobody will partner Singapore if it is not reliable, trustworthy nor capable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It is one thing to have ideas on how we can be relevant, how we can make a value contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But ultimately, nobody will partner Singapore if we are not reliable, trustworthy nor capable.

sections.label: Talking seriously needs real capabilities
sections.summary: Nobody will talk seriously to anyone without real capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Nobody will talk seriously to anyone without real capabilities.
